title: Chronos Solution Contract v2
description: What the solver returns to the API layer. Exactly one of `assignment` or `diagnosis` is present: a complete timetable with an itemised quality breakdown, or an infeasibility result carrying the minimal conflicting constraint set and the smallest relaxation that restores feasibility. A bare failure is not a legal response. Revision v2 (docs/contract-change-proposal-v2.md changes 2-6, signed 2026-10-06): an infeasible result also carries the deepest partial placement inside `diagnosis`, says how it was diagnosed (`method`), names constraints from a closed `kind` enum with the cells they concern, and gives a typed, verified relaxation; the quality block lists every loaded rule with an evaluation status and the rule-set version. Frozen contract 3 of 3.

status.description: 'solved' - every session was placed; 'infeasible' - no valid timetable exists under the given constraints, and a diagnosis explains why.

assignment.description: The timetable: one placement per session. Present only when status is 'solved'.

quality.description: Itemised score for the assignment. Present only when status is 'solved'. Rules and weights come from solver/rules/quality_rules.yaml - they are data, so a department can change a weight without a code change (CONTEXT.md section 2, rule 4).

score.description: Aggregate over EVALUATED rules only. Complete iff not_evaluated_rule_ids is empty. Higher is better.

rules_version.description: The `version` declared at the top of solver/rules/quality_rules.yaml for the rule set that produced this score.

not_evaluated_rule_ids.description: rule_ids whose breakdown entry has status not_evaluated. Non-empty means `score` is partial.

breakdown.description: One entry per rule in the loaded rule set - fired, zero, or not evaluated. Never only the rules that fired.

rule_id.description: Rule identifier as declared in quality_rules.yaml.

weight.description: Weight from the YAML. Known even when the rule could not run.

raw.description: The measured quantity before weighting, e.g. a count of violating occurrences.

penalty.description: The rule's contribution to the score, normally weight multiplied by raw.

explanation.description: Human-readable reason in institutional terms, e.g. 'AGN has 3 consecutive sessions on Monday'. Never a clause index or an internal id.

reason.description: Why the rule could not run, in institutional terms. A rule is not_evaluated only when its required input is absent, never because its result looks odd.

displaced.description: Sessions whose slot changed relative to the timetable being repaired. Empty for a fresh generate; populated by freeze-and-expand rescheduling, where minimising its length is the objective. Present only when status is 'solved'.

diagnosis.description: Why no valid timetable exists. Present only when status is 'infeasible'.

method.description: mus: a minimal unsatisfiable subset was extracted. search_exhaustion: complete search proved no timetable exists, but no explanation was extracted.

minimal_conflicting_set.description: The minimal unsatisfiable subset: constraints that cannot all hold at once, and from which removing any one restores satisfiability. Present and empty when method is search_exhaustion.

constraint_id.description: Stable identifier for the constraint, so a relaxation can name it.

description.description: Institutional terms only - named faculty, rooms and cohorts. Never clause indices, vertex numbers or internal ids. This string is shown directly to a timetable coordinator.

entity_ids.description: ids of the faculty, rooms, cohorts and sessions the constraint involves, for the UI to highlight. Ids live here; the description stays human.

slots.description: Every (day, period) cell this constraint is about, on the edge-list wall-clock axis. Empty when the constraint is not slot-specific. Individual cells, not a range: 'Monday 10.00-12.00' is [{day 0, period 1}, {day 0, period 3}], skipping break period 2.

suggested_relaxation.description: The smallest single change that restores feasibility - the constraint to drop or loosen, stated the way a coordinator would act on it. Required when method is mus, forbidden when method is search_exhaustion.

constraint_id.description: Identifier of the constraint to relax. Must be one of the constraint_ids in minimal_conflicting_set.

description.description: Institutional terms, e.g. 'Free room 603 at Wednesday 11.15 by moving the TE-Comp A DAA lab to Thursday'.

action.description: The relaxation as a typed change to the solver's input. Legal action_types per constraint kind are listed in contracts/relaxation_actions_v2.json.

params.description: Exact shape fixed per action_type by the allOf below (one branch per action_type).

verification.description: Result of re-solving with the action applied, within a configurable time budget. Never a boolean: 'checked and failed' and 'never checked' are different answers.

status.description: restored: the re-solve found a complete timetable. still_infeasible: it proved infeasibility again (a second, independent conflict exists). timeout: the budget ran out before either answer - 'could not confirm', never 'fixed'. not_attempted: only for MANUAL actions.

runtime_ms.description: Wall-clock time of the verification solve. null iff status = not_attempted.

allOf.description: MANUAL cannot be auto-applied, so it alone is never verified.

partial_placement.description: Diagnostic only - NOT a timetable. The deepest consistent partial assignment the search reached before proving infeasibility: the partial with the most sessions placed, ties going to the first reached in the solver's deterministic search order. Never to be published, scored or edited.

unplaced_session_ids.description: Sessions not in partial_placement. Never empty: an infeasible result with nothing unplaced is a contradiction.

allOf.description: Exhaustive search proves infeasibility but explains nothing: no conflicting set, no relaxation.
A MUS names at least one constraint and the relaxation for it.

metadata.description: Run statistics. Always present, for both outcomes, so an infeasible run is still measurable and reportable in the benchmark harness.

algorithm.description: Which algorithm produced this result, e.g. 'welsh-powell-greedy', 'backtracking+forward-checking+mrv', 'freeze-and-expand'.

sessions_assigned.description: Vertices successfully coloured. Equals sessions_total when status is 'solved'.

slots_used.description: Distinct slots the assignment occupies - the chromatic number achieved. null when no assignment was produced.

backtracks.description: Backtracking steps taken, for the complexity analysis. null when the algorithm does not backtrack.

allOf.description: A solved result carries an assignment, its quality breakdown and its displacement list, and carries no diagnosis.
An infeasible result carries a diagnosis and nothing that could be mistaken for a timetable or its score.

id.description: Stable opaque string identifier, matching the ids supplied in the edge-list payload.

period.description: Index on the edge-list wall-clock period axis.

slot_ref.description: One (day, period) cell on the edge-list wall-clock axis.

period.description: Starting period on the edge-list wall-clock grid. A session of duration n occupies this period and the next n-1 periods in teaching order.

room_id.description: Physical room. When the session sits in a sub-room, this is the parent room and sub_room_id names the partition.

sub_room_id.description: Sub-room within room_id, e.g. the '702-A' half of room 702. null when the session occupies the whole room.

placement.description: One session placed in one slot and room.

kind.description: Constraint class - only constraints the solver enforces (proposal section 5.1). FACULTY_CLASH, COHORT_CLASH, ROOM_CLASH: two sessions joined by a FACULTY / COHORT / ROOM edge may not share a slot. ROOM_OCCUPANCY: one session per room or sub-room per slot; a parent room in use locks its sub-rooms and vice versa. ROOM_CAPACITY: cohort head count <= room capacity. ROOM_TYPE: requires_lab => room.is_lab. FACULTY_UNAVAILABLE: declared or absence-derived blackout slots. PINNED_BLOCK: slots held by immovable blocks. LAB_CONTIGUITY: a lab block's sessions start together and run over a contiguous teaching-order chain. FIXED_SLOT: a pre-assigned session stays in its slot. The search outcomes UNSATISFIABLE_DOMAIN and INFEASIBLE_INSTANCE are not constraints and are not members.

params_unfix_slot.description: Release a frozen or pre-assigned session: its fixed_slot becomes null.

params_relax_faculty_availability.description: Remove these slots from the faculty member's declared unavailability. The backend refuses slots that come from a recorded absence.

params_relax_pinned_block.description: Remove one entity from one slot's pinned occupancy. Coordinator/admin only.

params_manual.description: No machine-applicable change; a person acts on the relaxation's description.
